lemmas.statement: The ring of Gaussian integers Z[i] is not a field, providing a primary algebraic obstruction to recovering M_n(C) from M_n(Z[i]) in finite report contexts.

The finite presented carrier and its quotient structure do not admit the spectrum or density of the continuous infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, formalizing the gap between finite and continuum QM carriers.

A self-adjoint matrix over Z[i] need not possess Gaussian-integer eigenvalues, because the characteristic polynomial discriminant can be a quadratic non-residue (specifically non-square in Z), preventing roots in Z[i].

near_misses.claim: The gap between finite M_n(Z[i]) and finite M_n(C) is removable via polynomial lifting for small dimensions.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Non-existence of root in Gaussian Integer

open_obligations: Lack of mechanism to construct the completion of finite presented carrier to an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space
Formal proof that Z[i] is not a field (Z has no element 2)
Verification that the selection of finite quotient fails to replicate continuum limit
